name: Curtiss-Wright CW-1 Junior
summary: Tiny 1930s parasol-wing pusher intended as an affordable 'Model T of the air'; about 270 were sold and only a few still fly.

wings: Parasol monoplane: the wing is mounted above the fuselage on struts
engines: Small three-cylinder Szekely radial mounted on top of the fuselage behind the wing
Two-blade pusher propeller on the upper fuselage surface
fuselage: Open cockpit with pilot and passenger in tandem
Short, narrow fuselage with the engine mounted high behind the occupants
tail: Conventional fixed tail with a tailwheel

tellTales: Parasol-wing monoplane with the propeller pushing from the top of the fuselage
Tiny open-cockpit aircraft with the engine above and behind the cockpit
Small strut-braced wing overhead and no engine in the nose

confusedWith.howToTell: The Cub has a tractor engine and propeller in the nose and a high wing attached to the fuselage; the CW-1 Junior has a pusher propeller on top of the fuselage.
The Aeronca C-3 has a tractor engine in the nose and an enclosed cockpit; the Junior has a pusher engine behind an open cockpit.
